text:
alice_support: customer C-9142 reporting intermittent 5xx/504s on hosted inference since 10:12 UTC. p99 tail latency >12s, lots of queue growth. they attached sample ids req_abc123 req_def456
ops-bot: alert: hosted-api.request_queue.depth(us-west-2) = 2387 for 14m, backlog growth rate +120/s :warning:
kevin_sre: assigning, taking a look at traces. any repro curl or full request example?
alice_support: pasted the request body and headers in ticket. seq length ~1500 tokens for these samples. customer says stream hangs then gateway 504.
maya_backend: pulling traces -> I see continuous-batcher backlog accumulating. dequeue latency climbing, batch formation timeouts hit. snippet from logs:```
2026-03-17T10:14:02Z batcher.INFO batch_create delay=340ms queue_depth=1984
2026-03-17T10:14:35Z batcher.WARN dequeue_latency.p99=6.3s backlog=2200
2026-03-17T10:15:01Z gateway.ERROR request_timeout id=req_abc123 route=hosted-west status=504
```
sahil_infra: this looks like queue saturation from a small set of very long-sequence requests. continuous_batcher.max_queue_depth currently 2000 in hosted-west pool, so once we hit that we start early-rejecting or delaying which causes long tail and gateway timeouts.
kevin_sre: can you repro locally against staging? run a burst of long-seq requests hitting same shard. try this curl (will fork a few threads):
```bash
for i in {1..200}; do \
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-open-3b","input":"<long prompt repeated>"}' &\
done
wait
```
maya_backend: reproduced on staging. batcher queue climbs, dequeue stalls, p99 dequeue ~7s, and gateway times out at 10s for some requests.
nora_product: customer is on hosted tier (not Dedicated). they can't flip headers. need a customer-facing workaround ASAP.
julie_support: updated customer with acknowledgement and ETA ~20m, asked if they can temporarily reduce concurrency.
sahil_infra: short-term mitigation options:
- increase continuous_batcher.max_queue_depth for hosted-west pool from 2k -> 4k (quick config flip)
- enable overflow routing to fallback model-variant (lower-latency) for that tenant
- apply per-tenant rate limit to the offending tenant to keep queue healthy
- add header "x-prefer-low-latency: true" which disables chunked batching (but customer can't set)
kevin_sre: I'll do the config flip + enable overflow routing for tenant-id t-c9142. executing playbook now.
ops-bot: /runbook apply batcher-adjust --pool hosted-west --param max_queue_depth=4000 --who kevin_sre
ops-bot: runbook started, task id rb-8721
maya_backend: after bump (10:28 UTC) queue depth dropped to ~680 within 3m, p99 dequeue down to 1.8s, token emission unchanged. some residual 5xx from upstream gateway timeouts while drains finish.
julie_support: customer C-9142 reports improvements, latency largely recovered, they still saw 1x 504 during the mitigation window. thanked them and left note.
kevin_sre: follow-ups:
- create postmortem with root cause = long-seq tenant causing continuous-batcher backlog -> queue depth limit triggered -> increased dequeue latency and gateway timeouts
- permanent fixes: dynamic per-tenant queue caps, adaptive routing to low-latency pool for long seqs, and better early-detection alerting on per-tenant backlog growth
nora_product: I'll coordinate prioritization with product for the routing change.
alice_support: marking incident resolved for now, keeping monitoring alerts at p99 < 3s for 1h before closing. thanks all :thumbsup:
